entries.5d83889fd09553ec: Semiconductors are made by shining light through photomasks, the master plates that carry circuit patterns, and projecting the image onto wafers. A single defect in a master plate would be transferred to every chip printed from it, so the master plates and their material, mask blanks, require inspection. Lasertec’s main field is this area, and it developed, respectively, the world’s first EUV mask blank defect inspection/review equipment using EUV light (wavelength 13.5nm) in April 2017 and the world’s first Actinic EUV patterned mask defect inspection equipment in September 2019. The technology is described as “optomechatronics, which fuses optical application technology at its core with peripheral technologies such as electronics, precision mechanics and image processing,” and its foundations include confocal optical systems, DUV (deep ultraviolet) optical systems, EUV (extreme ultraviolet) optical systems and optical interferometry technology. Research and development expenses in the fiscal year ended June 2026 were ¥16,292 million.

entries.dd4569db47c7b331: These are inspection and measurement equipment used in semiconductor manufacturing processes. They include equipment that detects defects in photomasks, the original plates bearing circuit patterns, and in mask blanks, their material, as well as equipment that inspects defects in semiconductor wafers. In April 2017, the company developed EUV mask blank defect inspection/review equipment using EUV light (wavelength 13.5 nm), and in September 2019 it developed actinic EUV pattern mask defect inspection equipment; each was developed for the first time in the world. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended June 2026 was ¥168,090 million, accounting for the majority of revenue of ¥230,485 million. Revenue fell 17.2% compared with the prior year, but the company explains this as the effect of low orders in the previous year. Orders for the current year were ¥172,216 million (up 208.5% year on year), and the order backlog at year-end was ¥301,303 million.

entries.eae186e52c7767ec: Operating profit in the fiscal year ended June 2026 was ¥105,259 million, down 14.3% from the previous fiscal year. Ordinary profit fell 9.7% to ¥107,895 million, and net income attributable to owners of the parent fell 8.5% to ¥77,485 million. Against revenue of ¥230,485 million and operating profit of ¥105,259 million, the company states as its basic management policy that it aims to “maintain an operating margin of 20% or more even under market contraction and build a robust financial and business foundation that makes continued growth investment possible.” The Fab-lite strategy, which involves owning few factories and concentrating on development, and the Global Niche Top strategy, which involves choosing markets that are hard to enter, are linked to this profit structure.
entries.ec5278e0af2c8c2e: This business makes inspection and measurement equipment that uses light-based technology to examine defects and conditions of objects. The annual securities report describes it as “a single segment that designs, manufactures and sells inspection and measurement equipment,” and there is only 1 reportable segment. Lasertec Corporation designs and manufactures the equipment; sales in North America and Europe are handled by consolidated subsidiary Lasertec U.S.A., Inc., and sales in Japan and Asia are handled by the company. After-delivery services are handled by Lasertec U.S.A., Inc. for North America and Europe, Lasertec Korea Corp. for South Korea, Lasertec Taiwan, Inc. for Taiwan, Lasertec China Co., Ltd. for China, Lasertec Singapore Pte. Ltd. for Singapore and Malaysia, and the company for Japan and other Asia. For the fiscal year ended June 2026, revenue was ¥230,485 million, ordinary profit was ¥107,895 million, and the number of employees was 1,335. Its customers are concentrated among companies that make advanced semiconductors: sales to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited were ¥49,244 million (21.4% of total sales), sales to Intel Corporation were ¥47,692 million (20.7%), and sales to Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd. were ¥46,528 million (20.2%), and the three companies combined account for 62.3%. Revenue by region was: South Korea ¥66,075 million, United States ¥51,610 million, Taiwan ¥45,854 million, other Asia ¥31,056 million, Japan ¥28,127 million, and Europe ¥7,759 million.
entries.edee0b8d21e79e06: Revenue in the fiscal year ended June 2026 was ¥230,485 million, down 8.3% from the previous fiscal year. The company explains that, although order intake for the current year recovered to ¥237,504 million, up 125.7% from the previous year, revenue declined because order intake in the previous year was low. By product, semiconductor-related equipment was ¥168,090 million (down 17.2%), services ¥58,646 million (up 36.5%) and other products ¥3,747 million (down 32.5%); only services grew. Because equipment takes time from order to delivery, order intake and revenue in a given year do not line up. In its medium-term management plan, the company states that it aims to shorten lead time, which was 1.5 to 2 years when the plan was formulated, to 0.5 to 1.5 years.
